cases.question: Did loss of measured motion response interrupt progress?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for the declared command-motion computation and incomplete for unique physical identity.

allowed_evidence.fact: Median delivered command was 0.31 m/s from 14 to 22 s.
Median delivered odometry was 0.01 m/s over the same interval.
The calibrated healthy measured speed was 0.29 m/s.
No accepted-actuation, contact, or wheel-motion feedback was retained.

required_units.text: The declared interval supports a command-to-motion discrepancy.
Unique actuator, contact, or mobility identity remains unresolved.

cases.candidate_answer: Yes. From 14–22 s, the 0.31 m/s delivered command coincided with only 0.01 m/s delivered odometry versus the 0.29 m/s healthy response, establishing the declared command-to-motion discrepancy. Its actuator, contact, or mobility identity is unresolved.

cases.question: Did a command-to-motion discrepancy prevent continuation?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for the declared discrepancy test and action result.

allowed_evidence.fact: The declared computation found no required sequence of low-response windows.
The navigation action succeeded.
One FollowPath attempt, zero failures, and zero recovery invocations were retained.

required_units.text: Reject the discrepancy premise under the declared test.
The action succeeded with one attempt and no failure or recovery.

cases.candidate_answer: No. The declared discrepancy test did not trigger, and the action succeeded after one FollowPath attempt with no failure or recovery invocation.

cases.question: Did a command-to-motion discrepancy cause the recorded recoveries?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for the declared discrepancy test and recovery counts, but not a physical cause.

allowed_evidence.fact: No required sustained low-response sequence was observed.
Three FollowPath attempts, two failures, and two source-qualified Wait invocations were retained.
The action succeeded.

required_units.text: The discrepancy premise is not supported.
Recovery events do not establish an unobserved physical mechanism.

cases.candidate_answer: The record contains recoveries, but the declared command-motion test did not trigger. Those recovery events therefore do not establish a command-to-motion discrepancy or its physical cause.

cases.question: What execution mechanism occurred, and did it prevent eventual continuation?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for discrepancy, later measured response, and final action status.

allowed_evidence.fact: From 9 to 16 s, delivered command median was 0.27 m/s and delivered odometry median was 0.00 m/s.
From 19 to 20 s, delivered odometry median was 0.25 m/s.
The action succeeded.

required_units.text: A bounded discrepancy occurred.
Measured response later returned and the action succeeded.

cases.candidate_answer: A command-to-motion discrepancy occurred from 9–16 s, but it did not prevent eventual continuation: measured response returned to 0.25 m/s at 19–20 s and the action succeeded.

cases.question: Did commanded motion fail to produce measured motion?
cases.evidence_completeness: Command samples are complete; the independently measured motion stream is absent.

allowed_evidence.fact: Delivered commands above 0.20 m/s were retained for 11 s.
No odometry or other independent motion measurement was retained.

required_units.text: Commands were delivered.
The discrepancy cannot be determined without measured motion.

cases.candidate_answer: Commands above 0.20 m/s were delivered, but no independent motion stream was retained. A command-to-motion discrepancy cannot be established or rejected from this packet.

cases.question: What do the command and odometry streams establish?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for delivered streams only.

allowed_evidence.fact: The capture received Nav2 command messages.
The capture independently received odometry messages.
The record does not prove downstream actuator acceptance or Nav2 consumption of odometry.

Actuator acceptance and Nav2 consumption are not established.

cases.candidate_answer: The capture establishes delivered command and independently delivered odometry streams. It does not establish downstream actuator acceptance or that Nav2 consumed the odometry.

cases.question: Was wheel slip the physical cause of the response loss?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for response loss; no wheel rotation or contact evidence is retained.

allowed_evidence.fact: Measured speed fell below 10 percent of the healthy response during sustained commands.

cases.candidate_answer: The record supports a command-to-motion response loss, not wheel slip specifically. Without wheel rotation, contact, or actuator-current evidence, slip remains one unresolved alternative.

cases.question: Did the configured low-response threshold trigger?
cases.evidence_completeness: Complete for the threshold and computed disposition.

allowed_evidence.fact: The threshold requires three consecutive windows below a 0.20 response ratio.
Only two consecutive qualifying windows were observed, and disposition was not_triggered.

required_units.text: The configured trigger did not fire.
Two qualifying windows were fewer than the required three.

cases.candidate_answer: No. Although two windows were below the 0.20 ratio, the configured rule required three consecutive windows, so the recorded disposition was not_triggered.

cases.question: What recovery sequence is source-qualified?

allowed_evidence.fact: The hash-bound recovery child is Wait.
Two Wait IDLE-to-RUNNING transitions and three FollowPath attempts were retained.
The policy sequence does not identify a physical cause.

required_units.text: Two source-qualified Wait invocations and three attempts were retained.
The sequence does not establish a physical cause.

cases.candidate_answer: The hash-bound policy and transitions qualify two Wait invocations across three FollowPath attempts. That software sequence does not identify the physical reason for recovery.
